companyBasic.title: Company Basic Profile
companyBasic.desc: Get the registration and shareholder picture of a target company in one go
companyBasic.prompt:
Go to Tianyancha, search for and open the company page of "{company}" — the bottom of the company page contains all data dimensions of the company; collect every dimension.

[Execution Requirements]
- Collect dimension by dimension: every dimension shown at the bottom of the page must be captured;
- If not logged in, prompt the user to log in (tell the user in the conversation to complete login in the fetch browser panel), then continue after login — never skip or substitute with other sources.

[Output] After collecting all dimensions, organize the data into a Markdown report saved to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation, sectioned by page dimension.

companyDeep.title: Company Deep Dive
companyDeep.desc: Equity penetration and legal risks — a thorough pre-investment check
companyDeep.prompt:
Run a pre-investment deep dive on "{company}": equity penetration, actual controller, related companies, and judicial risks.

[Information Requirements]
- Equity and judicial data are time-sensitive: rely on live retrieval; start from Tianyancha, Qichacha, China Judgements Online, the Enforcement Information website, and Credibility China, but you are not limited to these entries;
- Mark unreachable layers as "Not publicly disclosed" — never guess to complete the chain.

[Output Format] Save a Markdown report to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# "{company}" Deep-Dive Report
## 1. Equity Penetration
List the ownership chain upward from "{company}" layer by layer (indented list, stake per layer) down to natural-person / state-owned / listed-company endpoints.
## 2. Actual Controller
Conclusion + basis (voting chain / agreements); when the basis is thin, give the most likely control structure marked "to be verified".
## 3. Related Companies
Companies sharing the controller, cross-shareholdings, or overlapping executives (name + relation type).
## 4. Judicial Risks & Operational Abnormalities
Newest first: cause/case number, execution/dishonest status, role in the case, source link; if none, say so explicitly.

[Discipline]
- Every judicial entry must carry a case number or accessible source — no vague statements;
- Separate "risk signals" from normal business information; neither exaggerate nor omit;
- Never fabricate shareholders, stakes, or cases.

sentiment.title: Company News Scan
sentiment.desc: 30 days of coverage in one sweep, positive vs negative at a glance
sentiment.prompt:
Scan public sentiment coverage of "{company}" from the last 30 days, grouped as positive/negative/neutral. Anchor on today's date and look back 30 days; anything outside the window is out of scope.

[Search Requirements]
- Coverage must come from live retrieval — the last 30 days are absent from any model's knowledge; answering from memory is a task failure. Start from news outlets, trade media, regulatory announcements, and public social discussions, but you are not limited to these;
- When a repost and the original coexist, trace to the first publication.

[Output Format] Save a Markdown report to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# "{company}" Sentiment Scan (YYYY-MM-DD ~ YYYY-MM-DD)
## 1. Positive
Each: date | title/one-line summary | source link.
## 2. Negative
Same format, plus a one-line impact note (which business / scale / credibility).
## 3. Neutral
Same format.
## 4. Summary
Overall volume and tilt, the single most concerning negative item, trend note.

[Discipline]
- Every entry must carry an accessible source link; drop entries without one;
- Classify conservatively: uncertain items go to Neutral — never pad a category to fill the structure;
- If a category is empty, state "None found this period" explicitly — never fabricate or exaggerate.

competitor.title: Competitor Watch
competitor.desc: Track a competitor's product, market, and funding moves
competitor.prompt:
Summarize "{competitor/product}" moves from the past month: product launches, market moves, and funding news. Anchor on today's date and look back 30 days.

[Search Requirements]
- Moves must come from live retrieval — the last month is absent from any model's knowledge; answering from memory is a task failure. Start from product launch channels, trade media, funding databases, and official announcements (website/official account), but you are not limited to these.

[Output Format] Save to the task workspace and output in full in the conversation:
# "{competitor/product}" Moves (YYYY-MM-DD ~ YYYY-MM-DD)
List newest first, one subsection per item:
### MM-DD | [Product] / [Market] / [Funding] / [Org] (pick one)
- Summary: 2-3 sentences on what happened;
- Source: an accessible link.

## Takeaways
Up to 3 lines: the single most important move, and what it hints for the competitive landscape.

[Discipline]
- Every entry must carry an accessible source link; drop entries without one;
- When official statements and media interpretation conflict, follow the official announcement and note the difference;
- If nothing public this period, say "No public moves found" honestly — never pad with old news.

industryEvents.title: Industry Investment Events
industryEvents.desc: A weekly list of investment events, each with a company profile
industryEvents.prompt:
Compile a weekly investment-event briefing for the "{industry}" sector. Anchor on today's date and look back 7 days; anything outside the window is out of scope.

[Search Requirements]
- Event facts (date, round, amount, investors) must come from live web retrieval — the last 7 days are absent from any model's knowledge; answering from memory is a task failure. Start from keyword combos like "{industry} funding", "{industry} raises", "{industry} Series A/B", "{industry} strategic investment" and sources such as 36Kr, IT Juzi, Zero2IPO, Pedata, and official company announcements, but you are not limited to the listed entries.
- For company profiles, prefer public information from live retrieval; use materials already in the task knowledge base or workspace when available; supplement with built-in knowledge only for well-known companies you are confident about, and never contradict retrieval results. Never fabricate business figures under any circumstance.

[Output Format] Save a Markdown document to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# {industry} Investment Events Weekly (YYYY-MM-DD ~ YYYY-MM-DD)

## 1. Events of the Week (newest first, one subsection per event)
### MM-DD | Company (Round, Amount)
- Company profile: 2-3 sentences — core business and products, founding year or scale, and its position within the "{industry}" sector;
- Segment: the niche it plays in;
- Investors: lead and follow-on investors; mark "Undisclosed" honestly when missing;
- Why it matters: one line on why this event deserves attention (omit if information is thin);
- Source: an accessible link.

## 2. This Week's Takeaways
3-5 one-line highlights: largest deal, most active investor, sector heat.

[Discipline]
- Every event must carry an accessible source link; drop entries without one.
- Quality over quantity: aim for 5-15 events; if nothing is found, honestly state "No new public investment events found this week" — never pad the list.
- Strictly enforce the 7-day window: letting last month's news slip in is the worst failure of this task.

industryLeads.title: Investment Lead Scan
industryLeads.desc: Mine public info for actionable investment-promotion leads
industryLeads.prompt:
Mine public information for investment-promotion leads around the "{industry}" sector from the past month: capacity expansion, relocation, new subsidiaries, site selection. Anchor on today's date and look back 30 days.

[Search Requirements]
- Leads must come from live retrieval — the last month is absent from any model's knowledge; answering from memory is a task failure. Start from local government and industrial-park announcements, trade media, corporate investment announcements, and environmental-impact filings, but you are not limited to these.

[Output Format] Save a Markdown list to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# "{industry}" Investment-Promotion Leads (YYYY-MM-DD ~ YYYY-MM-DD)
List by lead value, one subsection each:
### Company | Type (Expansion/Relocation/New entity/Other)
- Lead details: what happened, scale/investment amount if disclosed, timeline;
- Follow-up angle: one line connecting the lead to what a host city could offer (optional; omit if information is thin);
- Source: an accessible link;
- Status tag: confirmed (filed/announced) vs intent/rumor.

## Lead Summary
The 1-2 leads to prioritize and why.

[Discipline]
- Every lead must carry an accessible source link; drop entries without one;
- Quality over quantity: aim for 5-15 leads; if nothing is found, state it honestly — never fabricate;
- Strictly enforce the 30-day window: letting older news slip in is the worst failure of this task.

industryPolicy.title: Industry Policy Scan
industryPolicy.desc: Policy moves in {industry} over the past 30 days, with takeaways and impact per item
industryPolicy.prompt:
Scan public policy developments around the "{industry}" sector from the last 30 days: industrial policies, planning documents, draft regulations, and enforcement moves issued by national ministries, local governments, and regulators. Anchor on today's date and look back 30 days; anything outside the window is out of scope.

[Search Requirements]
- Policy information must come from live retrieval — the last 30 days are absent from any model's knowledge; answering from memory is a task failure. Start from ministry websites, official gazettes, policy databases, and trade-media reposts, but you are not limited to these;
- For reposted policies, always trace to the issuing agency's original text, noting the issuer and document number (if any).

[Output Format] Save a Markdown report to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# "{industry}" Policy Scan (YYYY-MM-DD ~ YYYY-MM-DD)
List newest first by publication date, one subsection per policy:
### MM-DD | Policy Name (Issuing Agency)
- Policy essentials: 2-3 sentences — core content, scope, effective date / comment deadline;
- Impact on "{industry}": one line — favorable / adverse / neutral, with a reason;
- Source: an accessible link to the original text.

## Policy Summary
Up to 3 lines: the single most important policy move, and any compliance / application window to prepare for early.

[Discipline]
- Every entry must carry an accessible source link; drop entries without one;
- Distinguish "issued" from "open for comment" — never present a draft as enacted policy;
- If nothing is found this period, state "No public policy moves found" honestly — never pad with old policies.

regionPolicy.title: Regional Investment-Policy Scan
regionPolicy.desc: Investment-promotion and industry-support policies of {region} over the past 30 days
regionPolicy.prompt:
Scan public investment-promotion and industry-support policies of "{region}" from the last 30 days: investment-promotion measures, industry support funds, land/facility incentives, talent programs, and new business-environment policies. Anchor on today's date and look back 30 days; anything outside the window is out of scope.

[Search Requirements]
- Policy information must come from live retrieval — the last 30 days are absent from any model's knowledge; answering from memory is a task failure. Start from the local government website, government social-media accounts, the investment-promotion agency's official account, and authoritative media reposts, but you are not limited to these;
- For reposted policies, always trace to the issuing agency's original text, noting the issuer and document number (if any).

[Output Format] Save a Markdown report to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# "{region}" Investment-Policy Scan (YYYY-MM-DD ~ YYYY-MM-DD)
List newest first by publication date, one subsection per policy:
### MM-DD | Policy Name (Issuing Agency)
- Policy essentials: 2-3 sentences — who qualifies, the strength of support (funding/tax/land/talent), application conditions and deadlines;
- How to use it: one line on how a host city could leverage this policy (benchmarking / pitch material / enterprise services);
- Source: an accessible link to the original text.

## Policy Summary
Up to 3 lines: the policy most worth pitching externally, and one with an application window to race for.

[Discipline]
- Every entry must carry an accessible source link; drop entries without one;
- Distinguish "issued" from "open for comment" — never present a draft as enacted policy;
- If nothing is found this period, state "No public policy moves found" honestly — never pad with old policies.

ddChecklist.title: Due Diligence Checklist
ddChecklist.desc: Draft a four-dimension DD checklist in minutes
ddChecklist.prompt:
Draft a four-dimension due diligence checklist (Business/Financial/Legal/Compliance) based on public information about "{company}" and "{focus areas}".

[Approach]
- First quickly retrieve "{company}"'s public profile (business model, scale, litigation and penalty records) to tune the emphasis of each dimension; if retrieval is limited, generate a generic draft from "{focus areas}" alone and note at the top "not tailored with public info";
- Dimensions touched by "{focus areas}" get extra weight, addressed item by item.

[Output Format] Save a Markdown checklist to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# "{company}" DD Checklist Draft
## 1. Business / 2. Financial / 3. Legal / 4. Compliance
Within each dimension list check items by priority, each as:
- [ ] Item name — what to verify and why it matters (one line); tag (seen in public info / to verify in DD)

## How to Use
Positioning of the draft, suggested order of document requests, mapping to "{focus areas}".

[Discipline]
- This is a draft for humans to iterate: prefer listing an extra "to verify" item over dropping an awkward one;
- Public info can only support "seen" tags — it never replaces DD conclusions;
- Never fabricate "confirmed" facts.

businessModel.title: Business Model Breakdown
businessModel.desc: Five dimensions of how a company makes money
businessModel.prompt:
Break down "{company}"'s business model: how it makes money and why it keeps making money.

[Information Requirements]
- Prefer public materials from live retrieval (official site, prospectus/annual report, in-depth coverage, industry analyses); use task knowledge base or workspace materials when available;
- For dimensions with thin material, reasoned inference from industry common sense is allowed but must be tagged "inference" with its basis — never present inference as fact.

[Output Format] Save a Markdown report to the task workspace and output it in full in the conversation:
# "{company}" Business Model Breakdown
## 1. Customers
Who pays: segments; whether payer and user differ.
## 2. Value Proposition
What problem it solves, why it gets chosen.
## 3. Revenue Structure
How it charges: revenue mix, pricing; cite sources for any share figures.
## 4. Cost Structure
Where money goes: major cost items, scale-economy clues.
## 5. Moat
Why it lasts: brand/network effects/switching costs/cost advantage/licenses — assess each.
## One-line Summary
How it earns and what defends it, plus the most fragile link of the model.

[Discipline]
- Keep "confirmed" and "inference" distinguishable throughout;
- Cite sources for key figures;
- Never fabricate revenue, share, or other operating numbers.

fileOrganize.title: Batch File Organizer
fileOrganize.desc: Sort workspace files by your rules automatically
fileOrganize.prompt:
Organize the files in the task workspace by "{rule}" (e.g. by type/by date) and produce a verifiable change log.

[Approach]
- Scan all files in the workspace and design the grouping per "{rule}";
- Execute the moves once the plan is set; move only — never delete or edit file contents;
- On name conflicts at the destination, never overwrite — rename with a numeric suffix;
- Files you cannot classify go to a "pending" group; never force-classify.

[Output Format] Output in full in the conversation:
# File Organization Report
## Grouping Plan
How "{rule}" is operationalized (one line per group's criterion).
## Change Log
| File | Original Path | New Path |
One row per moved file.
## Pending & Exceptions
Unclassified files and why; conflict handling records.

[Discipline]
- The change log must match the actual moves one-to-one — no missing entries;
- Do not touch hidden or system files.

dataSummary.title: Data Summary
dataSummary.desc: Aggregate a file into a stats table by your criteria
dataSummary.prompt:
Read "{file name}" in the task workspace and compute statistics by "{aggregation criteria}", outputting a table.

[Approach]
- First check readability and data shape (columns, row count, types); surface anomalies (nulls/malformed/duplicates) before computing;
- If "{aggregation criteria}" is ambiguous, state your interpretation and assumptions; compute the most common reading and also give the alternative;
- Compute with exact calculation — never eyeball or estimate.

[Output Format] Output in full in the conversation:
# "{file name}" Data Summary
## Data Overview
Total rows, field notes, data-quality issues found.
## Results
Table per "{aggregation criteria}" (self-explanatory headers); key numbers must reconcile with the overview.
## Criteria & Assumptions
Interpretation of the criteria, assumptions made, excluded data and why.

[Discipline]
- Every number must come from the actual file contents — never estimate to fill;
- Excluded or corrected data must be disclosed explicitly — never silently dropped.
